layout.what: La cocina's room (cocina-kit.js), cut open as La sala: of its four walls the two far ones stand (the left one on x = 0, the back one on y = 0), cut at 4.95 (round 2: higher than the kit's 3.2, this set's own override round its call of cocinaBuild, for the tall window) with the plain dark backdrop above; the checker floor runs off the picture. Along the back wall from the corner, the counter (the kit's cupboards and white top) to past the right edge, the sink set into it near the corner, its tap at the wall; over it the big window (the kit's, view "patio": sky and a cloud, the yard's cream wall, the hedge), its frame standing out of the wall, the reveal the wall's thickness, its sill a ledge. Against the left wall, a little way from the corner, the fridge, its front looking +x, its door hinged on its far edge (open, it stands out into the room at the fridge's side, its inner face seen); the stool on the floor in front, where the frog stands
layout.why: the brief and page 11 decision 9: the set stands on the world's axes, nothing square to the camera; the kit fixes the room's plan (the corner at (0, 0), the walls on its axes). The old picture had the fridge, the counter and the window side by side on one flat wall: on a world axis a wall falls half a row a pixel, so the fridge (left of the counter, standing as low as the counter's foot) cannot share the counter's wall. The fridge stands on the left wall, the counter and the window on the back wall: both feet stay near their old rows where people stand at them, and the counter's top passes its old row (122) at x 170, the middle of what stands on it; to either side it falls half a row a pixel (CT: whatever stands on it moves to that row at its old x, as El banco's sitters to SY). The fridge is 3.15 high (1.4 times abuela, the old one was 2.3 times her) and 2.65 wide, so that it stands whole in the view, its door open too; its two shelves hold the four old places side by side as the old, moved down to where they show whole through its opening (HUECO), above the heads of whoever stands before it. The window is as wide as the old one and as tall (62 rows where the family stands outside: z 1.6 to 4.7), its glass's bottom on the old sill's row at x 154: whoever stands outside shows through it as through the old one, cut at the chest by the sill, the sky and the yard's wall round their head; the yard wall's top on its slope (MU), whoever stands outside with their feet on PA

front.how: the old background (fondo: the fridge, the counter, the window) was drawn before everyone, and the stool was in the sorted list; now each is a set thing. Every item the sprite layer draws owns the pixels it drew last; at the entry of each front part (after everyone in the sorted list, and after what nevera() draws in the fridge) the set's own pixels of the part are drawn again where they are nearer to the camera than the item that owns the pixel: bakedZ[i] > v / COS - (row + .5 - OY) * tan(30 deg) / S, v = (x + y) / R2 of the point the item stands on (the floor under (x, y - 1); a thing on the counter, the sill, a shelf or the fridge's top: that surface under (x, y - 1) at its height; the frog on the stool: its top). Whoever stands outside the window is clipped to the outside (clips) and nothing is drawn again over them. "Behind a thing" is that depth test, not a row
